T: A boy, a pelican and the Coorong.
D: A boy living with his reclusive dad on the wild South Australian coast raises an orphaned pelican called Mr Percival.
P: Serve the fish when Hideaway Tom brings in the catch.
S: Fingerbone Bill teaching Mike about the land
Bush damper baked in the coals, with butter and golden syrup. Rub 60g butter into 450g self-raising flour, add 300ml milk and shape a round.
Pippis cooked with garlic, chilli and parsley, the shellfish dug from the Coorong sands. Soak 1kg pippis in salted water for an hour.
M: Pan-fried fish with chips and lemon, the catch of the day from the shack on the dunes.
W: a cold night in the beach shack
Soft dumplings simmered in a golden syrup sauce, a shack-friendly pudding. Rub 50g butter into 200g self-raising flour, add 1 egg and a little milk.
K: the campfire at the beach shack
Strong black tea with milk and sugar. Boil 1.2L water, add 6 tea bags and let it stew for 5 minutes.

s.note: Fingerbone Bill teaching Mike about the land
s.how: Rub 60g butter into 450g self-raising flour, add 300ml milk and shape a round. Bake at 200C for 30 minutes until it sounds hollow. Serve with butter and golden syrup.
Soak 1kg pippis in salted water for an hour. Fry 3 garlic cloves and a chilli in olive oil, add the pippis and 100ml white wine, cover and cook until they open. Toss with parsley.

m.how: Bake 1kg frozen chips. Dust 4 white fish fillets in seasoned flour and fry in butter and oil for 3 minutes a side. Serve with lemon wedges and tartare sauce.

w.note: a cold night in the beach shack
w.how: Rub 50g butter into 200g self-raising flour, add 1 egg and a little milk. Drop spoonfuls into a simmering sauce of 150g golden syrup, 100g brown sugar and 500ml water and cook covered 20 minutes.

d.note: the campfire at the beach shack
d.how: Boil 1.2L water, add 6 tea bags and let it stew for 5 minutes. Pour into mugs with milk and sugar. Make it just before the film starts and keep the jug cold.
